(Newswires) DJIA 
Apple (AAPL) – The tech giant is struggling to push its music unit due to the high charges that must be paid to artists. (WSJ) Boeing (BA) – Korean Air, and other co. customers, are to inspect Boing 737 engines by November following the fatal incident reported by Southwest Airlines (LUV) which saw a fan unravelling from the engine. (Newswires) Home Depot (HD) – The co. is to increase tech units by 1,000 as part of a USD 11bln project aimed to extend its brick-and-mortar retail. (Newswires) Nike (NKE) – More senior executives left the retail giant abruptly, including Singh and Tawiah who were ‘forced to leave’. (WSJ) S&P500 
Tech names – US moves to halt sales from China’s telecom equipment makers. (NY Times) BlackRock (BLK) – The co. will acquire Tennenbaum Capital Partners, terms have not been disclosed. (Newswires) CBS (CBS) / Viacom (VIAB) –The former considers the legal risks of increasing the bid for Viacom as fear over shareholders’ call for legal action emerges. (FT) Ford (F) – The automaker announced a non-emergency services for medical purposes named GoRide, aimed at improving services for patients’ medical appointments. (Newswires) Lockheed Martin (LMT) – The defence names Sikorsky has partnered with German companies in its bid to win the EUR 4bln heavy lift helicopter contract from Berlin. (Newswires) Southwest Airlines (LUV) – The airline confirmed the fatal incident involving Flight 1380 which was diverted in Philadelphia after an issue over the number one engine was reported. (Newswires) Time Warner (TWX) / AT&T (T), – Lawyers stating the two may have gained an edge in the merger following the fight with lawyers and economists as the two have exposed weakness in the Trump administration’s lawsuit. (Newswires) Xerox (XRX) – Carl Icahn and Darwin Deason, both top shareholders in the co., suggested alternatives to its proposed merger with Fujifilm, which included a plan for the company to monetise some assets. (Newswires) NASDAQ 100 
Activision (ATVI) – The game co. is to launch ‘Call-of-Duty: Black Ops 4’ which will only allow for multiplayers and no single-player feature will be included, but will include a battle Royale mode, according to two sources. (Kotaku) Alphabet (GOOGL) – YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki is looking for new ways to improve relations with video creators. (Newswires) Amazon (AMZN) – The retail giant will launch the International Shopping Feature as part of its Shopping App enabling customers to purchase among more than 45mln items that can be delivered to their countries from the US. Separately, the co. and Best Buy (BBY) will cooperate to launch the next generation of Fire TV Edition in the US and Canada. (Newswires) Amgen (AMGN) – The pharmaceutical announced results for Phase 3 Liberty Trial of Aimovig for the treatment of migraine which failed the previous two-four preventive trials. (Newswires) Facebook (FB) – The social media reported to have halted apps from obtaining private information only on April 4th and is said to have exposed users’ friends lists to companies. The co. said it would continue requiring people to accept targeted ads as a condition of its service, which may aid in keeping its business model intact. (The Telegraph/Newswires) JD.com (JD) – The co. is trying to attract more European luxury brands to its site, saying it offers faster delivery and better protection against fakes than its rival, Alibaba (BABA). (Newswires) Mylan (MYL) – Canada stated it is working with US FDA to access supplies of Mylan’s EpiPen due to a growing shortage that has skipped the US. (Newswires) Retailer names (AMZN, WMT, RTH) – US President Trump tweeted ‘states being cheated by online retailers’. (Newswires) Shire (SHPG) – The co, is facing disapproval over its CEO pay policy which offers a bonus of 780% of the salary. (Newswires) Tesla (TSLA) – The automaker aims at to produce 6,000 units Model 3 per week by June and is to hire hundreds of workers in its plant in California to achieve this target. (MarketWatch) Wynn Resorts (WYNN) – Largest shareholder Elain Wynn urges to co. to reorganise the board and improve governance following the sexual scandal of her ex-husband. Separately, the co. is looking to tighten loan protection on Macau on a USD 3.05bln facility offering. (Newswires) OTHER NEWS 
Alibaba (BABA) – The co. confirmed test for self-driving vehicles joining competitors Baidu (BIDU) and Tencent (TCEHY). (SCMP) Dolby (DLB) – The co. will cooperate with Jiny media to enhance cinema locations in China. (Newswires) Embraer (ERJ) – The co.’s CFO Jose Antonio de Almedia Filippo steps down and Nelson Salgado will succeed. (Newswires) Paycom (PAYC) – The co. elects new COO Jon Evans and CIO Brad Smith, effective April 16th. (Newswires) Riot Blockchain (RIOT) – The SEC has issued a subpoena to the company whose shares skyrocketed after changing its name. (CNBC) Scientific Games (SGMS) – The co. has launched Szerencsejatek Zrt, the largest online sports betting channel in Hungary. (Newswires) Scotts Miracle-Gro (SMG) – The co. is to purchase assets from Sunlight Supply which will improve the ability of its wholly owned subsidiary, SMG will pay USD 425mln in cash and USD 25mln in SMG equity to Sunlight Supply. (Newswires) Seadrill (SDRL) – A Judge in the US stated he would grant approval to the co.’s plan to exit its Chapter 11 bankruptcy. (Newswires) VMware (VMW) – Carl Ichan has obtained a medium stake in the co. which is said to be below 5%, according to people familiar with the matter. (CNBC) BROKER MOVES
